51589476.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to C-terminal human Katanin p60 (111 to 491 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli Rosetta (DE3) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR Experiment: 6.10. SPR Experiment. The binding affinity of the test compounds with the katanin protein was assessed utilizing a Biacore T200 system (GE Healthcare Biosciences, Sweden). The immobilization of katanin protein onto a CM5 chip was achieved through a standard amine-coupling procedure in 10 mM sodium acetate buffer. The test compounds were diluted in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) buffer supplemented with 0.05% Tween 20 and 5% DMSO to appropriate concentrations and subsequently injected over the chip surface following a predefined program. The K_D value, characterizing the binding affinity, was determined employing the Biacore T200 evaluation software (GE Healthcare).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Identification of katanin as a direct target of compound 21b. (A) Surface plasmon resonance analysis of interactions between 21b and katanin-N (n = 3). K_D values are expressed as mean ± SD for each compound from three independent experiments. Representative images from three independent experiments are shown. (B) Biotin-annexed probe 21b-biotin. (C) MCF-7 cell lysates were subjected to incubation with either biotin-conjugated negative control or 21b-biotin. Immunoblotting was performed to visualize the binding proteins. Representative images from four independent experiments are displayed. (D) Immunoblotting analysis demonstrated a decrease in katanin protein levels following treatment with Katanin (katanin) siRNA. Representative images from three independent experiments are presented. (E) The antiproliferative activities of 21b on MCF-7 (negative control) and siKatanin MCF-7 cells were examined by MTT assay (n = 3). Data shown are mean ± SD. ****p < 0.0001, ****p < 0.0001 vs the negative control.
